Case.description:
`practice_area` is a registry string validated against packs-api at
write time (ADR 0002) - which pack's lifecycle vocabulary `phase` is
read from. `timezone`, `jurisdiction`, and `county` are the court's own
clock (ADR 0005), required on every case and validated at write time
against zoneinfo and state-law-api's registries - a case without a
court clock is not a case case-api can compute deadlines against, so
none of the three has a default. Together the three are a `Venue`
(see `venue.py`); `venue` rebuilds one from the columns below - it
reads cleanly against this table's own `court` column, which means
something else entirely: the tribunal itself (ADR 0001, for example
"419th").
Case.title: Case

CaseParty.description:
`aliases` holds other names this party is known by in the record -
filings, transcripts, communications - so downstream matching (docket,
analysis) can resolve a mention to the right party (ADR 0005).
CaseParty.title: CaseParty

CourtOrder.description:
`kind` is a registry string validated against the case's practice
area pack at write time (ADR 0005) - what kind of order this is
(statute, standing order, temporary order, final order, ...).
`supersedes` is `[{order_id, provision_keys: list[str] | None}, ...]` -
the orders (and optionally the specific provisions within them) this
order supersedes; every `order_id` must belong to the same case,
enforced at write time rather than by a foreign key, since a
supersession can name only some of an order's provisions.
`provisions_locked`, once true, freezes the order's provisions: PUT
provisions and a PATCH touching kind/effective_start/effective_end/
supersedes are refused; the lock never goes back to false once set - an
irreversible decision, not a toggle. `provision_revision` is bumped on
a provisions PUT and on any PATCH that changes kind, effective_start,
effective_end, or supersedes - a change counter downstream readers can
use to know their cached copy is stale.
CourtOrder.title: CourtOrder

Provision.description:
One term of a court order, extracted or hand-entered (ADR 0005).
`provision_key` is writer-assigned and stable across a `PUT
.../provisions` replace - the replace matches existing rows by
(order_id, provision_key) so a provision's id, and anything keyed
off it, survives an edit that keeps the same key. `detection_rules` is
`[{rule_id, condition_type, parameters, severity, finding_type,
description_template}, ...]`, validated at write time against
analysis-api's condition-type registry and, for a
`communication_channel` rule, the practice area's pack platform
vocabulary.
Provision.title: Provision
